1	# Carbon-aware Compute Scheduling Market
2	
3	A backend service for a carbon-aware batch-compute scheduling market. The service will evolve around scheduling and migrating batch jobs using live energy mix, regional carbon intensity, execution cost, deadlines, and data-residency constraints.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	The initial public endpoint is `GET /health`, which returns JSON with `status: "ok"`.
14	
15	## Audit endpoint
16	
17	```bash
18	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN
19	```
20	
21	`--audit` and `--token` form a pair: both omitted leaves `GET /audit` a plain 404 like any other unknown path, while giving only one, an empty value or a repeated option is a usage error (exit status 2). When both are given, `GET /audit` serves read-only queries against the audit journal at `PATH`; clients cannot select another file.
22	
23	Requests must carry exactly one `X-Audit-Token` header whose value equals `TOKEN` (missing, blank or duplicated headers get 401, a mismatched value 403). The query string maps to `audit.search`: optional `cursor`, `limit` (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, default 100), `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. Unknown, repeated or empty parameters get 400 `invalid_request`. A missing journal gets 404 `audit_not_found`, malformed journal content 409 `audit_invalid`, and other I/O failures 503 `audit_unavailable`.
24	
25	## Multi-token scoped authorization
26	
27	```bash
28	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG
29	```
30	
31	`--auth` is an alternative to `--token`; the two are mutually exclusive, and enabling the audit endpoint requires exactly one of them (anything else is a usage error, exit status 2). `CONFIG` is a UTF-8 file whose every non-empty line is a six-element JSON array:
32	
33	```json
34	["name", "sha256-hex", grace_until, ops, stages, keys]
35	```
36	
37	- `name` — a unique non-empty label for the token.
38	- `sha256-hex` — the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the token's raw UTF-8 bytes; unique across records. The file never holds plaintext tokens.
39	- `grace_until` — `null` or a non-negative integer Unix second; the token stays valid while the current Unix second is not greater than it.
40	- `ops`, `stages`, `keys` — each either `"*"` (the filter may be omitted or take any legal value) or an array of distinct non-empty strings, in which case the request must carry that filter explicitly with a value in the array. Operation and stage scopes use the search filter domains (`copy`/`restore`; `成功`, `校验`, `执行`, `同步`, `回滚`); history keys match exactly.
41	
42	The whole file is validated at startup (any error exits with status 2 without listening) and re-read on every request, so a same-directory atomic replacement rotates tokens without a restart: add the new digest and set a grace cutoff on the old one. A configuration that cannot be read or validated after startup answers 503 `auth_unavailable`. Unknown or expired tokens get 403; a valid token whose request lacks a required in-scope filter gets 403 as well, after query-parameter validation (400) and before the audit file is ever opened.
43	
44	## Proof export endpoint
45	
46	```bash
47	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN --checkpoint CPATH
48	```
49	
50	`--checkpoint` enables `GET /audit/proof`, the online export of `audit_proof.export` against the fixed checkpoint `CPATH`; it may only be given together with `--audit` (alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error, exit status 2). Without it the proof path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path. Clients can never select the audit or checkpoint file through the query.
51	
52	The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order (401/403, 400 `invalid_request`, scoped filters 403, 503 `auth_unavailable`). The query takes a mandatory non-empty `generation` name, an optional `final` flag (exactly `true` or `false`, defaulting to `false`) and the usual `cursor`, `limit`, `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. A successful export answers 200 with the offline-savable proof object, its page computed from the same journal snapshot the proof seals. The proof object is version 2 and ends with `checkpoint_etag`: the strong entity tag of the checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint download serves — so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint snapshot, and any later anchor, closing or new generation rebinds the proofs that follow it. A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory gets 404 `proof_not_found` (the real paths never leak); an invalid chain, checkpoint, generation state or growth relation gets 409 `proof_invalid` and appends no anchor; locking or I/O failures get 503 `proof_unavailable` with the old checkpoint preserved.
53	
54	## Checkpoint snapshot endpoint
55	
56	With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.
57	
58	Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.
59	
60	The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.
61	
62	The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.
63	
64	## Offline bundle verification
65	
66	```bash
67	python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG [--trust-dir PATH]
68	```
69	
70	`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three mandatory options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.
71	
72	Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.
73	
74	The optional `--trust-dir PATH` keeps a persistent sequence of the snapshots this machine has accepted, so a whole-bundle replay of an older — otherwise self-consistent — pair is rejected as a rollback. Without the option the single-bundle verification above runs unchanged and no directory is created. With it, the existing verification completes first; then, under the trust directory's exclusive lock, the verified snapshot is compared with the retained chain head. The first use of a not-yet-existing directory establishes the trust anchor from the just-verified checkpoint and saves its raw bytes. A later bundle carrying the same strong tag is an idempotent replay: the proof is fully re-verified and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the latest trusted one — existing generations, anchors, fields and values must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may be appended — so an already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors, or a bundle that cannot continue the head fails verification. Each sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks the real predecessor relation from disk; tampered node content, chain digests or head relations are never repaired from the bundle in hand. Directory updates serialize across processes and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs, with the head committed last: any failure keeps the pre-call head, and leftover fragments never take part in any decision.
75	
76	On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding and malformed trust metadata), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, state, page, snapshot-binding or trust-sequence mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files, a missing trust-directory parent, or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.
77	
78	## Test
79	
80	```bash
81	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
82	```
83

With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.

Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.

The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.

The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.

## Offline bundle verification

```bash
python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG [--trust-dir PATH]
```

`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three mandatory options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.

Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.

The optional `--trust-dir PATH` keeps a persistent sequence of the snapshots this machine has accepted, so a whole-bundle replay of an older — otherwise self-consistent — pair is rejected as a rollback. Without the option the single-bundle verification above runs unchanged and no directory is created. With it, the existing verification completes first; then, under the trust directory's exclusive lock, the verified snapshot is compared with the retained chain head. The first use of a not-yet-existing directory establishes the trust anchor from the just-verified checkpoint and saves its raw bytes. A later bundle carrying the same strong tag is an idempotent replay: the proof is fully re-verified and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the latest trusted one — existing generations, anchors, fields and values must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may be appended — so an already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors, or a bundle that cannot continue the head fails verification. Each sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks the real predecessor relation from disk; tampered node content, chain digests or head relations are never repaired from the bundle in hand. Directory updates serialize across processes and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs, with the head committed last: any failure keeps the pre-call head, and leftover fragments never take part in any decision.

On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding and malformed trust metadata), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, state, page, snapshot-binding or trust-sequence mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files, a missing trust-directory parent, or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from . import audit_proof, auth
from .server import serve


class _Once(argparse.Action):
    """Optional argument that may be given at most once."""

    def __call__(self, parser, namespace, values, option_string=None):
        if getattr(namespace, self.dest, None) is not None:
            parser.error(f"{option_string} must not be given more than once")
        setattr(namespace, self.dest, values)


class _UsageError(Exception):
    """A verify-bundle usage error, reported as invalid_request."""


def _raise_usage(message: str) -> None:
    raise _UsageError(message)


def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    command = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="carbon_market")
    subcommands = command.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    server = subcommands.add_parser("serve", help="start the HTTP service")
    server.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    server.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
    server.add_argument(
        "--audit", action=_Once,
        help="audit journal file to expose at GET /audit")
    server.add_argument(
        "--token", action=_Once,
        help="token clients must send in the X-Audit-Token header")
    server.add_argument(
        "--auth", action=_Once,
        help="multi-token scoped authorization file for GET /audit, "
             "exclusive with --token")
    server.add_argument(
        "--checkpoint", action=_Once,
        help="proof checkpoint file to expose at GET /audit/proof, "
             "requires --audit")
    bundle = subcommands.add_parser(
        "verify-bundle",
        help="verify a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair offline")
    bundle.add_argument(
        "--checkpoint", action=_Once, required=True,
        help="downloaded checkpoint file")
    bundle.add_argument(
        "--proof", action=_Once, required=True,
        help="downloaded proof file")
    bundle.add_argument(
        "--etag", action=_Once, required=True,
        help="strong ETag the checkpoint download carried")
    bundle.add_argument(
        "--trust-dir", action=_Once,
        help="directory retaining the persistent checkpoint sequence "
             "that rejects whole-bundle replays of older versions")
    # Usage errors of this command surface as the compact invalid_request
    # failure object on stderr, not as argparse's usage text.
    bundle.error = _raise_usage
    return command


def _fail(code: str, status: int) -> None:
    # Failure objects are a single compact JSON line on stderr and never
    # carry paths, system messages or input content; stdout stays empty.
    sys.stderr.write(json.dumps({"error": code}, separators=(",", ":"))
                     + "\n")
    raise SystemExit(status)


def _verify_bundle(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    # The three mandatory options are required and may appear at most
    # once (argparse enforces both); an empty value, an empty
    # --trust-dir or a tag that is not one quoted 64-digit lowercase
    # digest is a usage error too, and no argument error may read the
    # input files.
    if not args.checkpoint or not args.proof or not args.etag \
            or (args.trust_dir is not None and not args.trust_dir) \
            or not audit_proof._ETAG_RE.fullmatch(args.etag):
        _fail("invalid_request", 2)
    try:
        result = audit_proof.verify_bundle(
            args.checkpoint, args.proof, args.etag,
            trust_dir=args.trust_dir)
        payload = json.dumps(
            {"valid": True, "etag": args.etag,
             "generation": result["generation"],
             "closed": result["closed"],
             "events": result["events"], "next": result["next"]},
            ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
    except audit_proof.BundleMismatchError:
        _fail("verification_failed", 4)
    except ValueError:
        _fail("invalid_bundle", 3)
    except OSError:
        _fail("bundle_unavailable", 5)
    # Success: one compact UTF-8 JSON line on stdout; stderr stays empty.
    sys.stdout.write(payload + "\n")


def main() -> None:
    command = parser()
    try:
        if sys.argv[1:2] == ["verify-bundle"]:
            # Extras left over after the subcommand are reported by the
            # top-level parser; route them to the same failure object.
            command.error = _raise_usage
        args = command.parse_args()
    except _UsageError:
        _fail("invalid_request", 2)
    if args.command == "serve":
        # --audit pairs with exactly one authorization method: the
        # single --token or the multi-token --auth file. Both omitted
        # keeps GET /audit a plain 404; --audit without a method, a
        # method without --audit, both methods at once, an empty value
        # or a repeated option is a usage error and exits with
        # argparse's status 2. --checkpoint only ever accompanies
        # --audit: alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error too.
        if args.audit is None:
            if args.token is not None or args.auth is not None \
                    or args.checkpoint is not None:
                command.error(
                    "--token, --auth and --checkpoint require --audit")
        else:
            if not args.audit:
                command.error("--audit must be non-empty")
            if (args.token is None) == (args.auth is None):
                command.error(
                    "--audit requires exactly one of --token and --auth")
            if args.token is not None and not args.token:
                command.error("--token must be non-empty")
            if args.auth is not None and not args.auth:
                command.error("--auth must be non-empty")
            if args.checkpoint is not None and not args.checkpoint:
                command.error("--checkpoint must be non-empty")
        if args.auth:
            # The whole configuration is validated before the port is
            # bound; any failure is a usage error with status 2.
            try:
                auth.load(args.auth)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
                command.error(f"invalid --auth file: {exc}")
        serve(args.host, args.port, audit_path=args.audit, token=args.token,
              auth=args.auth, checkpoint=args.checkpoint)
    elif args.command == "verify-bundle":
        _verify_bundle(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

131	same-directory temporary file that is written and fsynced, moved over
132	the checkpoint with :func:`os.replace` and followed by a directory
133	fsync. A commit failure therefore never leaves a new anchor behind nor
134	returns a proof; concurrent appenders serialize and each observes
135	either the complete previous checkpoint or the complete new one, and a
136	restarted process continues the same anchor chain from the persisted
137	checkpoint.
138	"""

234	@contextlib.contextmanager
235	def _file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
236	    # Same flock discipline as the journal: the companion lock file is
237	    # never unlinked and the kernel releases the flock on process exit.
238	    lock_path = realpath + ".lock"
239	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
240	    try:
241	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
242	        try:
243	            yield
244	        finally:
245	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
246	    finally:
247	        os.close(fd)

255	def _compact(payload: Any) -> bytes:
256	    # The journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention: compact separators,
257	    # non-ASCII written through. Used for every digest here.
258	    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),

263	    # The strong entity tag of a checkpoint snapshot: one double-quoted
264	    # string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the
265	    # complete bytes -- exactly the computation and quoting the
266	    # conditional download serves in its ETag header.

301	def _manifest(document: dict[str, Any]) -> list[list[Any]]:
302	    # The complete snapshot inventory: every audit key in journal order
303	    # paired with the exact digest its sealed chain gives it. Comparing
304	    # manifests item by item enforces "known events unchanged, only new
305	    # keys added" without trusting the journal bytes alone.
306	    chain = document["chain"]
307	    return [[audit_key, chain[audit_key][1]]
308	            for audit_key in document["events"]]

310	
311	def _validate_manifest(raw: object) -> list[list[Any]]:
312	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
313	        raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be a list of "
314	                                "[audit key, event digest] pairs")
315	    manifest: list[list[Any]] = []
316	    last_key: str | None = None
317	    for item in raw:
318	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2 \
319	                or not isinstance(item[0], str) or not item[0] \
320	                or not _is_digest(item[1]):
321	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest entries must be "
322	                                    "[non-empty key, 64-digit hex digest]")
323	        if last_key is not None and item[0] <= last_key:
324	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be ordered by "
325	                                    "key code point without repeats")
326	        manifest.append([item[0], item[1]])
327	        last_key = item[0]
328	    return manifest

330	
331	def _check_extension(old_manifest: list[list[Any]],
332	                     new_manifest: list[list[Any]]) -> None:
333	    # The old snapshot must survive key by key: every anchored key keeps
334	    # its exact digest, while new keys may land anywhere in code-point
335	    # order -- the manifests are compared as key/digest pairs, not by
336	    # position. Fewer entries (retreat), a missing old key (deletion) or
337	    # a changed digest under a known key (rewrite) all surface here.
338	    # Equal manifests (re-query or byte-level log rotation with same
339	    # events) are permitted by the caller and never reach this check.
340	    if len(new_manifest) <= len(old_manifest):
341	        raise BundleMismatchError("a generation only accepts snapshots "
342	                                  "that add new audit events")
343	    new_digests = {audit_key: digest for audit_key, digest in new_manifest}
344	    for audit_key, digest in old_manifest:
345	        if new_digests.get(audit_key) != digest:
346	            raise BundleMismatchError("a generation cannot rewrite, delete "
347	                                      "or reorder an already anchored event")
348	
349	
350	def _validate_checkpoint(data: object) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
351	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
352	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint root must be an object with "
353	                                "keys version and generations, in that "
354	                                "order")
355	    version = data["version"]
356	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
357	            or version != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
358	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported checkpoint version")
359	    generations_raw = data["generations"]
360	    if not isinstance(generations_raw, list):
361	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint generations must be a list")
362	    if not generations_raw:
363	        # export only creates a checkpoint together with its first
364	        # generation, so a persisted empty list is structural damage.
365	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint must carry at least one "
366	                                "generation")
367	
368	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
369	    generations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
370	    # The previous-anchor chain runs across the whole checkpoint: the
371	    # first anchor of a later generation names the last anchor of the
372	    # closed previous generation, so the stream never forks.
373	    previous: str | None = None
374	    for gen_position, generation_raw in enumerate(generations_raw):
375	        is_last_generation = gen_position == len(generations_raw) - 1
376	        if not isinstance(generation_raw, dict) \
377	                or list(generation_raw.keys()) != list(_GENERATION_FIELDS):
378	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must be an object "
379	                                    "with keys name and anchors, in that "
380	                                    "order")
381	        name = generation_raw["name"]
382	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
383	            raise BundleFormatError("generation name must be a non-empty "
384	                                    "string")
385	        if name in seen_names:
386	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not repeat")
387	        if generations and name <= generations[-1]["name"]:
388	            # Names open in strictly ascending code-point order; an
389	            # equal-or-earlier name is a repeat or a regression.
390	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not regress")
391	        seen_names.add(name)
392	        anchors_raw = generation_raw["anchors"]
393	        if not isinstance(anchors_raw, list) or not anchors_raw:
394	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must carry at least "
395	                                    "one anchor")
396	
397	        anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
398	        for index, anchor_raw in enumerate(anchors_raw):
399	            is_last_anchor = index == len(anchors_raw) - 1
400	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw, dict) \
401	                    or list(anchor_raw.keys()) != list(_ANCHOR_FIELDS):
402	                raise BundleFormatError(
403	                    "each anchor must be an object with keys manifest, "
404	                    "log_digest, head, previous, closed and digest, in "
405	                    "that order")
406	            manifest = _validate_manifest(anchor_raw["manifest"])
407	            if not _is_digest(anchor_raw["log_digest"]):
408	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor log_digest must be a "
409	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
410	                                        "digest")
411	            head = anchor_raw["head"]
412	            if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
413	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor head must be null or a "
414	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
415	                                        "digest")
416	            declared_previous = anchor_raw["previous"]
417	            if index > 0 and not _is_digest(declared_previous):
418	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor previous digest must be a "
419	                                        "64-digit hexadecimal digest")
420	            if declared_previous != previous:
421	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor previous digest does not "
422	                                          "continue the chain")
423	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw["closed"], bool):
424	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor closed must be a boolean")
425	            digest = anchor_raw["digest"]
426	            if not _is_digest(digest):
427	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor digest must be a 64-digit "
428	                                        "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
429	            expected = _anchor_digest(manifest, anchor_raw["log_digest"],
430	                                      head, previous, anchor_raw["closed"])
431	            if digest != expected:
432	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor digest does not match "
433	                                          "its content")
434	
435	            if anchors:
436	                earlier = anchors[-1]
437	                if earlier["closed"]:
438	                    raise BundleMismatchError("a closed anchor cannot be "
439	                                              "followed inside its "
440	                                              "generation")
441	                # Consecutive anchors either pin the same manifest (a
442	                # byte-level log rotation with the events intact, or the
443	                # closing anchor flipping the closed flag) or extend it
444	                # with new keys anywhere in code-point order while every
445	                # anchored pair survives; anything else is a rewrite.
446	                if manifest == earlier["manifest"]:
447	                    if head != earlier["head"]:
448	                        raise BundleMismatchError(
449	                            "a same-snapshot anchor cannot move the root "
450	                            "digest")
451	                    if anchor_raw["log_digest"] == earlier["log_digest"] \
452	                            and anchor_raw["closed"] == earlier["closed"]:
453	                        raise BundleMismatchError("a duplicate anchor "
454	                                                  "changes nothing")
455	                else:
456	                    _check_extension(earlier["manifest"], manifest)
457	            if anchor_raw["closed"] and not is_last_anchor:
458	                raise BundleMismatchError("only the last anchor of a "
459	                                          "generation may be closed")
460	
461	            anchor = {"manifest": manifest,
462	                      "log_digest": anchor_raw["log_digest"], "head": head,
463	                      "previous": declared_previous,
464	                      "closed": anchor_raw["closed"], "digest": digest}
465	            anchors.append(anchor)
466	            previous = digest
467	
468	        if not is_last_generation and not anchors[-1]["closed"]:
469	            # An open generation may only be the last one of the
470	            # checkpoint: any following generation proves it was closed.
471	            raise BundleMismatchError("a new generation can only start "
472	                                      "after the previous one is closed")
473	        generations.append({"name": name, "anchors": anchors})
474	    return generations

482	            f"checkpoint file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
483	    try:

507	def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
508	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
509	    try:
510	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
511	    finally:
512	        os.close(dir_fd)

514	
515	def _commit_checkpoint(realpath: str, directory: str, payload: bytes,
516	                       old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
517	    # Same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync --
518	    # with a rollback if anything fails after the replace, so a failed
519	    # commit never leaves the new anchor behind. The pre-call bytes are
520	    # staged back over the file (or the file removed when it did not
521	    # exist) and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive
522	    # lock is held; a failed rollback surfaces chained after the first
523	    # error.
524	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
525	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-proof-", suffix=".tmp")
526	    try:
527	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
528	            handle.write(payload)
529	            handle.flush()
530	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
531	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
532	    except BaseException as first:
533	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
534	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
535	        raise
536	    try:
537	        _fsync_dir(directory)
538	    except BaseException as first:
539	        audit._rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
540	        raise

574	def export(
575	    audit_path: str,
576	    checkpoint_path: str,
577	    generation: str,
578	    final: bool = False,
579	    cursor: str | None = None,
580	    limit: int = audit._DEFAULT_LIMIT,
581	    op: str | None = None,
582	    stage: str | None = None,
583	    key: str | None = None,
584	) -> dict[str, Any]:
585	    """Export a verifiable proof and anchor it in the checkpoint.
586	
587	    ``audit_path`` and ``checkpoint_path`` must be non-empty strings;
588	    ``generation`` must be a non-empty string and ``final`` a boolean.
589	    The search arguments follow :func:`carbon_market.audit.search`. All
590	    argument errors raise ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
591	
592	    A missing audit journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; so does a
593	    missing parent directory of a checkpoint that must be created. A
594	    version 1 journal, an incomplete digest chain, a malformed
595	    checkpoint, a repeated generation name or an export that reopens a
596	    past generation, an attempt to open a new generation while the
597	    previous one is still open, an export that deletes or rewrites
598	    events of the current generation, or any non-identical export of a
599	    closed generation raises ``ValueError``. Remaining locking or I/O
600	    failures raise ``OSError``.
601	
602	    Returns the offline proof dict: a version 2 envelope whose last
603	    field, ``checkpoint_etag``, is the strong entity tag of the
604	    checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- the same
605	    quoted SHA-256 the checkpoint download serves. A repeat of an export
606	    whose content and closed state are identical appends nothing and
607	    returns a proof naming the same anchor and the unchanged snapshot's
608	    tag. With ``final=True`` the appended anchor closes
609	    generation -- it may pin the same snapshot -- after which only the
610	    identical idempotent export (``final=True``) is accepted.
611	    """
612	    for value in (audit_path, checkpoint_path):
613	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
614	            raise ValueError("audit_path and checkpoint_path must be "
615	                             "non-empty strings")
616	    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not generation:
617	        raise ValueError("generation must be a non-empty string")
618	    if not isinstance(final, bool):
619	        raise ValueError("final must be a boolean")
620	    _check_params(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
621	
622	    audit_real = os.path.realpath(audit_path)
623	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
624	    checkpoint_store = _get_store(checkpoint_real)
625	    with checkpoint_store.lock:
626	        # Hold the journal's shared lock and the checkpoint's exclusive
627	        # lock together until the commit lands, so audit.record cannot
628	        # rotate the journal while its bytes are sealed into an anchor.
629	        with audit._file_lock(audit_real, shared=True):
630	            # Read inside the shared flock exactly like the read-only
631	            # audit queries: a racing audit.record is observed as one
632	            # complete document or the other, never a half-replaced
633	            # file. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError.
634	            with open(audit_real, "rb") as handle:
635	                raw = handle.read()
636	            document = _parse_journal_snapshot(audit_real, raw)
637	            with _file_lock(checkpoint_real):
638	                generations, old_bytes = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
639	                if generations is None:
640	                    generations = []
641	
642	                params = _params_dict(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
643	                # Compute the page from the exact bytes in hand; this is
644	                # the same filter/pagination audit.search applies.
645	                result = _search_document(document, params)
646	                manifest = _manifest(document)
647	                head = document["head"]
648	                log_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
649	                names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
650	
651	                def identical(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
652	                    return (item["manifest"] == manifest
653	                            and item["log_digest"] == log_digest
654	                            and item["head"] == head)
655	
656	                if generation in names:
657	                    position = names.index(generation)
658	                    if position != len(generations) - 1:
659	                        # A past generation can never be reopened.
660	                        raise ValueError("a past generation cannot be "
661	                                         "exported again")
662	                    current = generations[position]
663	                    anchors = current["anchors"]
664	                    last = anchors[-1]
665	
666	                    if last["closed"]:
667	                        # Once closed the only accepted export is the
668	                        # idempotent one: final stays true and the
669	                        # snapshot is byte-for-byte the same -- events,
670	                        # log bytes and root head. The query may differ,
671	                        # since verify recomputes the page from the
672	                        # embedded log and parameters.
673	                        if not final or not identical(last):
674	                            raise ValueError("a closed generation only "
675	                                             "accepts the identical "
676	                                             "idempotent export")
677	                        return _build_proof(
678	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
679	                            head, True, last["digest"],
680	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
681	
682	                    # Still open. Same events, same bytes, same head and
683	                    # not closing: the duplicate export appends nothing
684	                    # and returns the proof of the latest anchor. The
685	                    # manifest must equal the latest anchor's, so an
686	                    # older snapshot cannot mask a retreat.

795	def _search_document(document: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) \
796	        -> dict[str, Any]:
797	    # Recompute audit.search's result from an in-memory document so
798	    # verify never needs the journal file itself.
799	    cursor = params["cursor"]
800	    limit = params["limit"]
801	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
802	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
803	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
804	            continue
805	        if not audit._matches(event, params["op"], params["stage"],
806	                              params["key"]):
807	            continue
808	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
809	        if len(matches) > limit:
810	            break
811	    if len(matches) > limit:
812	        page = matches[:limit]
813	        return {"events": page, "next": page[-1][0]}
814	    return {"events": matches, "next": None}

817	def _verify_proof(generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
818	                  clean: dict[str, Any],
819	                  checkpoint_real: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
820	    # The cross-checks every verified proof must pass against one
821	    # checkpoint snapshot: the named generation and anchor must be
822	    # recorded, the embedded log bytes must hash to the anchored log
823	    # digest and reparse as a sealed version 2 journal whose manifest
824	    # and root head the anchor pins, and the page must recompute from
825	    # the embedded log and parameters. Every failure here is a
826	    # mismatch, never a format error.
827	    names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
828	    if clean["generation"] not in names:
829	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof generation is not recorded in "
830	                                  "the checkpoint")
831	    generation = generations[names.index(clean["generation"])]
832	    anchor = next((item for item in generation["anchors"]
833	                   if item["digest"] == clean["anchor_digest"]), None)
834	    if anchor is None:
835	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof anchor is not recorded in the "
836	                                  "checkpoint")
837	
838	    params = clean["params"]
839	    raw = clean["log_bytes"].encode("utf-8")
840	    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != clean["log_digest"]:
841	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log bytes do not match their "
842	                                  "log digest")
843	    if clean["log_digest"] != anchor["log_digest"]:
844	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log digest is not bound to the "
845	                                  "anchor")
846	    try:
847	        document = audit._parse_document(checkpoint_real, raw)
848	        audit._ensure_chain(document)
849	    except ValueError as exc:
850	        raise BundleMismatchError(str(exc)) from exc
851	    if document["version"] != 2:
852	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof requires a sealed version 2 "
853	                                  "audit journal")
854	    if clean["head"] != document["head"] \
855	            or anchor["head"] != document["head"]:
856	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof root digest does not match the "
857	                                  "journal")
858	    if _manifest(document) != anchor["manifest"]:
859	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof event manifest does not match "
860	                                  "the anchor")
861	    if clean["closed"] != anchor["closed"]:
862	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof closed state does not match "
863	                                  "the anchor")
864	
865	    recomputed = _search_document(document, params)
866	    if recomputed != clean["result"]:
867	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof result does not follow from "
868	                                  "the embedded log and parameters")
869	    return {"events": clean["result"]["events"],
870	            "next": clean["result"]["next"],
871	            "generation": clean["generation"],
872	            "closed": anchor["closed"]}

875	def verify(checkpoint_path: str, proof: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
876	    """Verify an exported proof solely against the checkpoint.
877	
878	    The journal is not opened: the proof carries the journal's raw
879	    bytes, parameters and result. ``checkpoint_path`` must be a
880	    non-empty string and ``proof`` an object previously returned by
881	    :func:`export`.
882	
883	    The checkpoint bytes are read under the shared lock and their
884	    strong tag is recomputed and confronted with the proof's bound
885	    ``checkpoint_etag`` before anything else: a proof exported against
886	    another snapshot -- older or newer -- mismatches. The embedded log
887	    bytes must hash to the proof's log digest, parse as
888	    a complete version 2 journal whose event manifest and root head
889	    match the anchor the proof names in the named generation of the
890	    checkpoint, and the page must recompute from the embedded log and
891	    parameters. Every anchor chain in the checkpoint is rechecked as
892	    well. Success returns
893	    ``{"events": ..., "next": ..., "generation": ..., "closed": ...}``
894	    -- the original search result together with its generation and
895	    closed state.
896	
897	    A missing checkpoint raises ``FileNotFoundError``; a proof without
898	    the snapshot binding (version 1) or any other structural problem
899	    raises ``BundleFormatError``; any proof or checkpoint mismatch --
900	    including changed log bytes, parameters, page content, cursor, any
901	    digest or a stale snapshot tag -- raises ``BundleMismatchError``;
902	    other I/O failures raise ``OSError``. Both error types are
903	    ``ValueError`` subclasses.
904	    """
905	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_path, str) or not checkpoint_path:
906	        raise ValueError("checkpoint_path must be a non-empty string")
907	
908	    clean = _validate_proof(proof)
909	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
910	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
911	        # One locked snapshot: the tag is recomputed from the exact
912	        # bytes that are then parsed and validated, so a racing
913	        # replacement can only yield a self-consistent outcome.
914	        try:
915	            with open(checkpoint_real, "rb") as handle:
916	                raw = handle.read()
917	        except FileNotFoundError:
918	            raise FileNotFoundError(
919	                f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} does not exist"
920	            ) from None
921	        if clean["checkpoint_etag"] != _strong_tag(raw):
922	            raise BundleMismatchError(
923	                "proof checkpoint_etag does not bind the checkpoint "
924	                "snapshot in hand")
925	        generations = _parse_checkpoint(checkpoint_real, raw)
926	    return _verify_proof(generations, clean, checkpoint_real)

1043	def _load_trust_chain(trust_real: str) -> tuple[
1044	        list[dict[str, Any]], str, dict[str, Any], bytes, bytes,
1045	        list[dict[str, Any]]] | None:
1046	    # Read and re-validate the retained sequence from disk. Returns None
1047	    # when no head was ever committed -- a first use, or a crashed first
1048	    # use that left only unreferenced files behind. Anything referenced
1049	    # by the head that is missing, malformed or inconsistent is a
1050	    # failure of the retained evidence and is never repaired here.
1051	    head_path = os.path.join(trust_real, "head.json")
1052	    try:
1053	        with open(head_path, "rb") as handle:
1054	            head_raw = handle.read()
1055	    except FileNotFoundError:
1056	        return None
1057	    head_digest = _validate_head(_loads_trust(head_path, head_raw))
1058	
1059	    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1060	    seen: set[str] = set()
1061	    digest: str | None = head_digest
1062	    while digest is not None:
1063	        if digest in seen:
1064	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust chain contains a cycle")
1065	        seen.add(digest)
1066	        node_path = os.path.join(trust_real, "nodes", digest + ".json")
1067	        try:
1068	            with open(node_path, "rb") as handle:
1069	                node_raw = handle.read()
1070	        except FileNotFoundError:
1071	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust chain references a missing "
1072	                                      "node") from None
1073	        node = _validate_node(_loads_trust(node_path, node_raw))
1074	        if _node_digest(node["tag"], node["previous_tag"],
1075	                        node["checkpoint_digest"],
1076	                        node["previous_digest"]) != digest:
1077	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust node digest does not match "
1078	                                      "its content")
1079	        nodes.append(node)
1080	        digest = node["previous_digest"]
1081	    nodes.reverse()
1082	    for earlier, later in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
1083	        if later["previous_tag"] != earlier["tag"]:
1084	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust node predecessor tag does "
1085	                                      "not continue the chain")
1086	    head_node = nodes[-1]
1087	    snapshot_path = os.path.join(trust_real, "snapshots",
1088	                                 head_node["checkpoint_digest"] + ".json")
1089	    try:
1090	        with open(snapshot_path, "rb") as handle:
1091	            snapshot_raw = handle.read()
1092	    except FileNotFoundError:
1093	        raise BundleMismatchError("trust head checkpoint snapshot is "
1094	                                  "missing") from None
1095	    if hashlib.sha256(snapshot_raw).hexdigest() != \
1096	            head_node["checkpoint_digest"]:
1097	        raise BundleMismatchError("trust head checkpoint bytes do not "
1098	                                  "match the chain")
1099	    trusted = _parse_checkpoint(snapshot_path, snapshot_raw)
1100	    return nodes, head_digest, head_node, head_raw, snapshot_raw, trusted

1103	def _check_strict_append(old_generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
1104	                         new_generations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
1105	    # The new checkpoint must be the trusted one plus only appended
1106	    # content: every retained generation survives untouched, the head
1107	    # generation keeps its anchors as a prefix, and at least one anchor
1108	    # or generation is added. The appended content's own legality was
1109	    # already established by the checkpoint validation of the bundle.
1110	    if len(new_generations) < len(old_generations):
1111	        raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint drops trusted generations")
1112	    for position, old_generation in enumerate(old_generations):
1113	        new_generation = new_generations[position]
1114	        if position < len(old_generations) - 1:
1115	            if new_generation != old_generation:
1116	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites a trusted "
1117	                                          "generation")
1118	        else:
1119	            if new_generation["name"] != old_generation["name"]:
1120	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites the "
1121	                                          "trusted head generation")
1122	            old_anchors = old_generation["anchors"]
1123	            if new_generation["anchors"][:len(old_anchors)] != old_anchors:
1124	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites trusted "
1125	                                          "anchors")
1126	    if len(new_generations) == len(old_generations) \
1127	            and len(new_generations[-1]["anchors"]) \
1128	            == len(old_generations[-1]["anchors"]):
1129	        raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint is not a strict append of "
1130	                                  "the trusted head")

1158	def _update_trust(trust_dir: str, etag: str, raw: bytes,
1159	                  generations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
1160	    # Compare the verified snapshot with the retained chain head and
1161	    # advance the head when it is a strict append-only successor. Runs
1162	    # under the trust directory's exclusive lock so concurrent
1163	    # verifications serialize: the successor advances the head once and
1164	    # a later-arriving older version fails against the moved head.
1165	    trust_real = os.path.realpath(trust_dir)
1166	    store = _get_store(trust_real)
1167	    with store.lock:
1168	        with _file_lock(trust_real):
1169	            if not os.path.isdir(trust_real):
1170	                # First use of a not-yet-existing directory. A missing
1171	                # parent surfaces as FileNotFoundError, either here or
1172	                # already from the lock file creation above.
1173	                os.mkdir(trust_real)
1174	                _fsync_dir(os.path.dirname(trust_real) or ".")
1175	            chain = _load_trust_chain(trust_real)
1176	            digest_hex = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
1177	            if chain is None:
1178	                # Establish the trust anchor from the just-verified
1179	                # checkpoint and save its raw bytes.
1180	                node = {"tag": etag, "previous_tag": None,
1181	                        "checkpoint_digest": digest_hex,
1182	                        "previous_digest": None}
1183	                head_old: bytes | None = None
1184	            else:
1185	                nodes, head_digest, head_node, head_raw, _, trusted = chain
1186	                if etag == head_node["tag"]:
1187	                    # Idempotent replay of the trusted head: the bundle
1188	                    # was fully re-verified above and the directory
1189	                    # stays untouched.
1190	                    return
1191	                if any(item["tag"] == etag for item in nodes):
1192	                    raise BundleMismatchError(
1193	                        "checkpoint replays an earlier trusted version")
1194	                _check_strict_append(trusted, generations)
1195	                node = {"tag": etag, "previous_tag": head_node["tag"],
1196	                        "checkpoint_digest": digest_hex,
1197	                        "previous_digest": head_digest}
1198	                head_old = head_raw
1199	            _ensure_dir(os.path.join(trust_real, "nodes"))
1200	            _ensure_dir(os.path.join(trust_real, "snapshots"))
1201	            # Snapshot and node are content-addressed and committed
1202	            # before the head, so a failure anywhere keeps the pre-call
1203	            # head and leaves only reusable complete files behind.
1204	            _ensure_file(os.path.join(trust_real, "snapshots",
1205	                                      digest_hex + ".json"), raw)
